classificationReport.bandRationale: All three are verification-completeness and cluster-hygiene gaps. Fork-verified end-state: 2.3 add/remove executes cleanly, zero unintended writes, old strategies fully drained before retirement, idempotent, no exploit path. No assets stolen/lost/compromised (fails C4 High). No protocol function or availability impact and no value leak with a realized attack path (fails C4 Medium: 2.3 itself succeeds and is safe). Each is a concrete spec/verification deviation or a non-obvious operator footgun with a described mis-operation scenario, which places it squarely in the QA/Low band per C4 ('state handling, function incorrect as to spec') rather than pure informational noise. Plausibility sub-category is N/A (Low band).

classifiedFindings.label: L-01
classifiedFindings.title: Saga 2.3 final verification omits the cushion-1 (skimmed-surplus) buffer check despite the protocol-wide 'one buffer' framing

classification.assetImpact: None at direct risk. Cushion-2 (the 10% strategy-level withholding to the staker) is independently in place and asserted; cushion-1 (the skimmed DOLA/USDC surplus that 2.2 step 8 transfers to the staker) is fungible idle balance the owner can re-transfer manually. No drain, no lock, no protocol availability impact — 2.3 itself runs and is safe.
classification.attackPath: N/A (no attacker). Mis-operation scenario: (1) 2.2 completes steps 1-7 but reverts/is interrupted at step 8 (the buffer transfer); (2) operator runs 2.3; (3) 2.3 _verify asserts only setAsideBufferSize==10 (cushion-2) and passes all 8 gates green; (4) migration is declared complete while the protocol-wide buffer is short by the entire skimmed surplus and no gate flagged it.
classification.likelihood: low - requires a partial/interrupted 2.2 at the specific step-8 transfer, an operational edge case, not a routine path.
classification.assumptions: Set-aside and buffer are ONE protocol-wide concept realized by two cushions (owner clarification). The final step is intended to assert end-state health.
classification.externalRequirements: An interrupted/partial 2.2 run (buffer transfer skipped) preceding 2.3.

classifiedFindings.rationale: C4 Low. No assets at risk and no availability impact: 2.3 succeeds, cushion-2 is asserted and independently in place, and the missing cushion-1 surplus is recoverable by a non-malicious owner. This is not High (no theft/loss path) and not Medium (no protocol-function/availability impact and no realized value leak). It sits in the QA/Low band as a verification-completeness / state-handling gap: the declared final gate over-trusts a green result because it never asserts cushion-1 landed nor that setAsideBufferRecipient==STAKER. It is a non-obvious operator footgun (Law 3) — a competent non-malicious operator would be surprised a green 2.3 verify does not cover the buffer concept end-to-end — so it is reportable at Low rather than suppressed, and concrete enough (real interrupted-2.2 scenario) to be Low rather than pure informational QA.

classifiedFindings.label: L-02
classifiedFindings.title: Saga 2.3 verify drops two plan-mandated end-state gates (minterV2 seeded; phUSD minter authority V1-off/V2-on) to log-only / unchecked
classifiedFindings.lineageNote: Adjacent to saga2.1 L-02 (fingerprint 7f11380101ffbe022b41d314, wont-fix, migrate:saga2.1-deploy). Distinct: 2.1 L-02 is 'deploy script lacks post-write asserts'; this is 'the declared FINAL verification step omits gates its own plan Section 5.4 says to assert all'. Triage should decide whether to extend the L-02 wont-fix posture or action the gate-completeness drift separately; routed to spec-conformance regardless so it stays visible to the owner.

classification.assetImpact: None at direct risk. If minter authority were mis-set (V1 still a minter, or V2 not), phUSD mint accounting could diverge from the intended V2-only regime, but that mis-set requires a 2.1 failure or a separate owner action and is independently surfaced by 2.1's own asserts. 2.3 itself writes nothing wrong here; it merely fails to re-assert.
classification.attackPath: N/A (no attacker). Faithfulness/process scenario: (1) 2.1 lands strategies/JSON but fails at the phUSD setMinter step (2.1 step 8), OR an owner later re-flips minter authority; (2) operator runs 2.3 expecting plan Section 5.4 'assert all' coverage; (3) 2.3 _verify never re-checks phUSD.minters(V1)==false / (V2)==true nor the USDe-client wiring, and demotes minterV2 principals to console.log; (4) the saga's declared final gate passes green without catching the divergence.
classification.likelihood: low - requires a prior 2.1 failure or a separate owner re-flip; the happy path is unaffected.
classification.assumptions: Plan-doc Section 5 Script 3 step 4 / Section 5.4 enumerates these as gates to 'assert all' and 2.3 is the declared final verification step.
classification.externalRequirements: A 2.1 partial failure at the setMinter step, or a subsequent owner action altering minter authority.

classifiedFindings.rationale: C4 Low, tagged faithfulness and routed to the spec-conformance report (F-S23-02). This is a Law-2 story/spec deviation: the step whose stated job is to 'assert all' final gates implements an incomplete superset of its own plan (phUSD setMinter V1-off/V2-on and USDe client wiring unchecked; minterV2 principals demoted to log-only). Per Law 2 it must not be buried in the QA/gas bundle — it is surfaced at honest severity in the dedicated spec-conformance channel. Severity stays Low: no standalone exploit, no asset/availability impact, and the underlying mis-set would itself require a 2.1 failure or separate owner action already covered by 2.1's asserts. The minterV2-principal log-only relaxation is a documented, defensible relaxation and not itself a defect; the unchecked phUSD/USDe gates are the reportable drift. It is also a non-obvious footgun (operator believes green 2.3 == plan 5.4 fully satisfied).

classifiedFindings.label: L-03
classifiedFindings.title: Superseded sibling DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA hardcodes the DEAD SYA (0x3bBE) and reads an empty deployments file — latent wrong-route footgun adjacent to 2.3
classifiedFindings.lineageNote: Prior YS-31 / Q-SYA-SEL lineage: dead pre-story-058 SYA 0x3bBE928340c61a65Cb6C4a87B3fb59B6f3F7606a, superseded by live 0x3C690EC3...8270. Surfaced as a residual cross-route hazard adjacent to 2.3, NOT a 2.3 defect (same-surface exception to 'do not surface other-scope items').

classification.assetImpact: None. No impact on the saga-2 flow itself — 2.3 uses the correct live SYA 0x3C69 and is the route in the npm flow. The superseded sibling, if run, accomplishes nothing (reverts on empty JSON or no-ops against the dead 0x3bBE instance); no value is moved, lost, or stolen.
classification.attackPath: N/A (no attacker). Cross-route footgun scenario: (1) operator picks the superseded ys-swap DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA.s.sol instead of (or in addition to) 2.3; (2) it hardcodes LIVE_SYA=0x3bBE (the DEAD pre-story-058 SYA) and reads the empty ys-swap-deployments.json; (3) the empty-JSON read reverts in practice, or — since 0x3bBE may still have code and a matching owner — the owner()/code.length preflight is not a guaranteed loud failure and it no-ops against the dead instance; (4) operator believes the old strategies were deregistered when they were not.
classification.likelihood: low - requires the operator to choose the wrong, superseded retirement route; the npm flow points at 2.3.
classification.assumptions: The two retirement routes coexist in the cluster and the superseded sibling still ships unquarantined with stale constants and an empty inputs file.
classification.externalRequirements: Operator running the superseded ys-swap retirement script rather than the saga-2 2.3 route.

classifiedFindings.rationale: C4 Low. No assets at risk and no availability impact on the audited saga-2 flow — 2.3 targets the correct live SYA and the superseded sibling, if mis-run, simply accomplishes nothing. Not High (no theft/loss) and not Medium (no protocol-function/availability impact). It is a QA/Low state-handling / dead-code landmine: a stale hardcoded DEAD-SYA constant plus an empty inputs file on a sibling that performs the same removeYieldStrategy operation on the same SYA-deregister surface 2.3 supersedes. It qualifies as Low rather than pure informational because the preflight is not a guaranteed loud failure (0x3bBE may retain code + matching owner), so an operator on the wrong route can believe deregistration succeeded when it did not — a non-obvious cross-route operator footgun (Law 3). Surfaced under the same-surface exception (reachable from the saga-2 retirement surface 2.3 owns), not an unrelated scope. No change needed to 2.3 itself; remediation is to quarantine/repoint the superseded sibling.
